definitions.gloss: to lose sight of, to lose track of
definitions.explanation: To no longer be able to see someone or something that one was watching or following. Used both literally (losing visual contact) and figuratively (losing one's sense of direction or purpose).

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}を{見失|みうしな}った。
examples.english: I lost sight of the suspect.

examples.japanese: {人混|ひとご}みの{中|なか}で{子供|こども}を{見失|みうしな}ってしまった。
examples.english: I lost sight of my child in the crowd.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しさに{追|お}われて、{自分|じぶん}が{本当|ほんとう}にやりたいことを{見失|みうしな}っていた。
examples.english: Caught up in busyness, I had lost sight of what I really wanted to do.

notes:
USAGE:
{見失|みうしな}う is a compound verb combining {見|み} (see) and {失|うしな}う (to lose). The figurative use — losing sight of one's goals, purpose, or identity — is very common, especially in expressions like {自分|じぶん}を{見失|みうしな}う (to lose sight of oneself).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犯人|はんにん}を{見失|みうしな}う: to lose sight of the suspect
- {目標|もくひょう}を{見失|みうしな}う: to lose sight of one's goal
- {自分|じぶん}を{見失|みうしな}う: to lose oneself
- {方向|ほうこう}を{見失|みうしな}う: to lose one's bearings
